rules.title: General
rules.description: Rules are guidelines; players may choose differently if they can justify it.

rules.title: Yearly order
rules.description: Calculate income â†’ marriage â†’ tax â†’ personal expenses â†’ rent/mortgage â†’ other expenses â†’ debt. Add what's left to savings or debt.

rules.title: Minimum-wage job
rules.description: $38,000/year; automatic success.

rules.title: Advanced job
rules.description: Roll 4-6 to earn $50,000/year.

rules.title: Career job
rules.description: Roll 4-6 to get the job. Required education must be completed.

rules.title: Work and school
rules.description: Until age 25, you may have full-time work or school plus part-time work or school.

rules.title: Marriage income
rules.description: Married players increase their combined income by 25% (multiply by 1.25).

rules.title: Personal expenses
rules.description: Pay 20% of after-tax income for food, phone, insurance, gas, and other personal expenses (multiply remaining income by 0.8).

rules.title: Children
rules.description: Each child costs $8,000/year.

rules.title: Living at home
rules.description: You may live at home until age 23.

rules.title: Home purchase
rules.description: The minimum down payment is 15%.

rules.title: Home prices
rules.description: Condo: $575,000; townhouse: $835,000; detached: $1,100,000.

rules.title: Mortgage
rules.description: Maximum 25 years at 0% annual interest. Calculate annual payments as (house price âˆ’ down payment) / payment years.

rules.title: Transportation
rules.description: Public transit costs $0; the minimum car purchase price is $5,000.

rules.title: Education
rules.description: Post-secondary education costs $8,000/year.

rules.title: Savings
rules.description: Savings earn 5% annually (multiply by 1.05).

rules.title: Debt
rules.description: Debt accrues 10% interest annually (multiply by 1.1).

rules.title: Debt versus savings
rules.description: After expenses, choose how much money to put toward debt; the rest goes to savings.

rules.title: Selling a house
rules.description: When you sell your house, you receive 75% of its equity (house value âˆ’ remaining mortgage).

rules.title: Divorce
rules.description: If you divorce, lose 50% of your savings and $5,000.

rules.title: Marriage
rules.description: Roll 4-6 to get married.

events.title: Car crash
events.description: Watch out! 1-3: Your car is totaled; add half its value to your savings. 4-6: That was close.

events.title: Lottery Win
events.description: You bought the right ticket at the right time. Add 1,000 Ã— your roll to savings.

events.title: Unexpected Inheritance
events.description: Great-Uncle Bob apparently liked you more than everyone else. 1-2: Gain $25,000. 3-6: Gain $10,000.

events.title: Found Money
events.description: You check an old account and discover money you forgot existed. 1-2: Gain $10,000. 3-6: Gain $5,000.

events.title: Tax Refund
events.description: Apparently you gave the government too much money. 1-3: Gain $10,000. 4-6: They kept it. Somehow.

events.title: Side Hustle
events.description: Your questionable idea actually makes money. 1-2: Gain $10,000. 3-6: Gain $5,000.

events.title: Lucky Break
events.description: Right place, right time. 1-2: Gain $5,000. 3-6: You were almost lucky. Nothing happens.

events.title: Garage Treasure
events.description: You find something valuable buried under 15 years of junk. 1-3: Gain $5,000. 4-6: Just garbage. Lots and lots of garbage.

events.title: Old Investment
events.description: That thing you bought years ago actually went up. 1-2: Gain $5,000. 3-6: You sold too early. Nothing happens.

events.title: Car Sale
events.description: Someone really wants your old car. 1-3: Gain $5,000. 4-6: They changed their mind.

events.title: Bonus!
events.description: Your boss noticed you actually showed up to work. 1-3: Gain $5,000. 4-6: Your boss noticed. That's it.

events.title: Home Repair
events.description: Your roof has decided that it doesn't like being a roof anymore. 1-3: Lose $5,000. 4-6: You caught it before it got expensive.

events.title: Car Repair
events.description: The check-engine light has evolved into a check-bank-account light. 1-3: Lose $5,000. 4-6: It was just the gas cap. You're saved.

events.title: Vet Bill
events.description: Your pet has discovered the most expensive way possible to be sick. 1-4: Lose $5,000. 5-6: False alarm! Your pet is fine.

events.title: Bad Investment
events.description: It sounded like a great idea at the time. It wasn't. 1-4: Lose $5,000. 5-6: You got out just in time.

events.title: Oops, That's Broken
events.description: You broke something that was working perfectly yesterday. 1-3: Lose $5,000. 4-6: You fixed it yourself. Somehow.

events.title: Emergency Expense
events.description: Life has presented you with an invoice. 1-3: Lose $10,000. 4-6: Insurance actually covered it.

events.title: Car Trouble
events.description: The mechanic says, 'Well... that's not good.' 1-3: Lose $10,000. 4-6: It was only a loose wire.

events.title: Lawsuit
events.description: Congratulations! You're involved in a legal dispute. 1-3: Lose $10,000. 4-6: You settle it without paying.

events.title: Roof Leak
events.description: It's raining inside now. That's generally considered bad. 1-4: Lose $10,000. 5-6: Your insurance saves you.

events.title: Medical Bill
events.description: You're fine! Your bank account isn't. 1-3: Lose $10,000. 4-6: Your insurance covers it.

events.title: Terrible Investment
events.description: You were promised guaranteed returns. They forgot to mention the guaranteed part was the loss. 1-4: Lose $10,000. 5-6: You listened to your gut and didn't invest.

events.title: Major Repair
events.description: The thing you hoped wouldn't break has broken. 1-4: Lose $25,000. 5-6: You found a cheap fix. Lose $5,000 instead.

events.title: Financial Disaster
events.description: Everything that could go wrong financially decided to happen at once. 1-4: Lose $25,000. 5-6: You dodge the worst of it. Lose $5,000.

events.title: The Expensive Mistake
events.description: 'How much could it possibly cost?' Famous last words. 1-3: Lose $25,000. 4-6: Lose $10,000.

events.title: Oops, A Baby
events.description: Positive! Probably! 1-3: Add 1 child. 4-6: Choose whether to add the child.

events.title: Unexpected Baby
events.description: The family just got a little bigger. 1-2: Add 1 child. 3-6: False alarm! No baby.

events.title: Baby Fever
events.description: You thought you were done. Apparently, your partner wasn't. 1-3: Add 1 child. 4-6: You talked them out of it.

events.title: Love at First Sight
events.description: You met someone who doesn't immediately run away after hearing about your finances. 1-3: Get married. 4-6: Choose whether to get married.

events.title: The Big Question
events.description: You popped the question. They said yes! Probably. 1-3: Get married. 4-6: You decide to wait.

events.title: Cheater!
events.description: Your partner catches you. 1-3: Divorce. 4-6: You went to counseling and worked it out.

events.title: We Need to Talk
events.description: You knew it wasn't going to be good when they started with those four words. 1-3: Divorce. 4-6: You work things out.

events.title: The Job Interview
events.description: Somehow they didn't notice you have no idea what you're doing. 1-3: Get a job. 4-6: You didn't get it.

events.title: Right Place, Right Time
events.description: Your friend knows a guy who knows a guy. 1-3: Get a job. 4-6: The guy doesn't know a guy after all.

events.title: Layoffs!
events.description: Corporate says you're 'part of the family.' Then they fire you. 1-3: Lose your job this year. 4-6: You made the cut. What did you do to make that happen?

events.title: Fired!
events.description: 'We're going in a different direction.' That direction apparently doesn't include you. 1-4: Lose your job. 5-6: You talk your way out of it.

events.title: Boss From Hell
events.description: You finally snap after your boss sends another email marked 'URGENT.' 1-3: Lose your job this year. 4-6: You apologize and keep your job.

events.title: The Company Closed
events.description: Your workplace is gone. Unfortunately, so is your paycheck. 1-4: Lose your job this year. 5-6: You transfer to another location.

events.title: Monday Morning
events.description: You wake up and realize you absolutely cannot do this job for another 30 years. 1-3: Lose your job this year. 4-6: Coffee fixes everything.

events.title: I Quit!
events.description: You hand in your resignation with absolutely no plan whatsoever. 1-3: Lose your job. 4-6: You realize you need the money and take it back.

events.title: Career Crisis
events.description: You stare at your career and think, 'Is this really it?' 1-2: Leave your career permanently. 3-6: You decide to stick with it.

events.title: Tripped
events.description: You trip over a slightly raised piece of concrete. 1-3: Lose 75% of your income this year; you're on disability this year. 4-6: 'Tis but a scratch.

events.title: Car Crash
events.description: Watch out! 1-3: Your car is totaled. 4-6: That was close.

events.title: Bad Luck
events.description: You somehow manage to injure yourself doing something completely normal. 1-3: You cannot work this year. 4-6: You're fine. Somehow.

events.title: Free Money!
events.description: The government, school, or some mysterious organization has decided to help you. 1-2: Free reroll. 3-6: They changed their mind.

events.title: Second Chance
events.description: That card was terrible. Pretend it never happened. 1-2: Free reroll. 3-6: Nope. You have to live with it.

events.title: Win a Car!
events.description: Congratulations! You now own a vehicle you didn't pay for. 1-2: Gain a car. 3-6: The dealership calls. It was a clerical error.

events.title: Car Giveaway
events.description: You entered a contest for a car and somehow actually won. 1-2: Gain a car. 3-6: You were the runner-up.

events.title: Car Theft
events.description: You go outside and discover your car has gone on an unscheduled vacation. 1-4: Lose your car. 5-6: You find it parked three blocks away.

events.title: Car Crash
events.description: You and your car had a disagreement with another vehicle. 1-4: Lose your car. 5-6: It can be repaired.

events.title: Engine Explodes
events.description: Your car has decided it would rather be a very expensive lawn ornament. 1-4: Lose your car. 5-6: Lose $5,000 instead.

events.title: Where's My Car?
events.description: You definitely parked it here... right? 1-3: Lose your car. 4-6: You find it. You just forgot where you parked.

events.title: The Mechanic
events.description: 'It's going to be cheaper to buy another car.' 1-4: Lose your car. 5-6: Lose $5,000 instead.

events.title: Education Setback
events.description: Your professor has discovered that you are, in fact, not finished. 1-3: Education delayed 1 year. 4-6: You convince them to let you finish.

events.title: Registration
events.description: Problem: You missed an important deadline. 1-3: Education delayed 1 year. 4-6: They make an exception.

events.title: Scholarship!
events.description: Someone looked at your tuition bill and decided to save you from it. 1-3: Education is free this year. 4-6: You got a partial scholarship. Pay half.

events.title: Free Tuition
events.description: Somehow, you found the magical phrase 'fully funded.' 1-2: Education is free this year. 3-6: You only get half off.

events.title: Bankruptcy
events.description: You have officially entered financial 'oops.' 1-4: Debt becomes $0, but you cannot buy a house or car for 3 years. 5-6: You avoid bankruptcy. Lose $25,000.

events.title: Promotion!
events.description: Your boss finally realizes that replacing you would be difficult. 1-3: Income increases by $10,000/year. 4-6: Your boss says 'maybe next year.'

events.title: Forced Sale
events.description: The bank, circumstances, or life itself says it's time to move. 1-4: Sell your house. 5-6: You manage to keep it.

events.title: Noticed Your Hard Work
events.description: You've been doing your job well enough that someone finally noticed (yeah right). 1-3: Income increases by $5,000/year. 4-6: Your boss gives you a pizza party instead.

events.title: The Brown-Noser
events.description: You brought your boss coffee for 4,245 consecutive days. It worked. 1-3: Income increases by $5,000/year. 4-6: Your boss starts asking for cream and sugar too. No raise.

events.title: House Flipper
events.description: You sell your house at the perfect time. 1-3: Sell your house and receive 110% of the equity. 4-6: Sell your house and receive 100% of the equity.
